subject.title: Steer mode does not inject messages mid-turn for main sessions

question: Should ordinary same-session visible messages in `messages.queue.mode: "steer"` be allowed to bypass channel/session admission lanes to reach active-run queue policy, and what safety boundary should govern that bypass across Discord, Telegram, and WebChat?
rationale: The remaining bug is real, but the safe fix point crosses channel ingress ordering, session/thread binding, first-turn setup, and one-writer session guarantees, so maintainer intent is needed before another automation lane changes the admission model.

options.title: Post-context steer admission
options.body: Allow ordinary messages to reach queue policy only after the channel has resolved the final session key/thread binding and can prove they target the active same-session run.

options.title: Command-only steering
options.body: Keep the current explicit `/steer`/control-command fixes and document that ordinary text will not bypass busy lanes even when queue mode is steer.

options.title: Broader concurrency redesign
options.body: Fold this into the same-session fast-lane/concurrent-turn design work instead of landing a narrower steer-mode admission fix now.

recommendation.title: Post-context steer admission
recommendation.body: Allow ordinary messages to reach queue policy only after the channel has resolved the final session key/thread binding and can prove they target the active same-session run.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice affects session admission and one-writer runtime policy where history and repository ownership point to steipete as the best routing owner.
